title: C strings: char arrays with a '\0' sentinel
expectedStdout:
length 12, sizeof 13
strcmp == 0 → equal contents
copied: Hello world!
as std::string: Hello world!
tryThis: Write `s == t` instead of `std::strcmp(s, t) == 0`: the compiler warns, because that compares two addresses, which always differ.
Make `buf` only 5 chars long and run with **ASan**: `strcpy` overflows the buffer (a classic security bug).
